# Camera Pose and Parameter Optimization

Also called: Joint Pose and NeRF Optimization, Unposed NeRF Training, Differentiable Registration

## Overview
This family of methods addresses the problem of optimizing Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) scene representations $\Theta$ and camera parameters (poses $P$ and intrinsics) simultaneously from a set of images without pre-computed Structure-from-Motion (SfM) data [7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md]. Unlike standard NeRF training which assumes fixed, known camera poses, these methods treat extrinsic and intrinsic parameters as learnable variables within the differentiable rendering loop [7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md]. They differ from sibling methods like [Training Ray Marching and Integration](2199-training-ray-marching-and-integration.md) by explicitly including pose gradients in the optimization graph, and from [Sparse View and Initialization Methods](9394-sparse-view-and-initialization-methods.md) by often starting from degenerate or random initializations rather than SfM outputs.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of differentiable rendering to compute gradients with respect to camera parameters.

1.  **Differentiable Ray Casting:** For each pixel $p$ in image $I_i$, a ray is defined by origin $o_i$ and direction $d_{i,p}$. These are functions of the camera pose parameters (rotation $R_i$, translation $t_i$) and intrinsics (e.g., focal length $f$).
    $$ o_i = t_i $$
    $$ d_{i,p} = R_i \begin{pmatrix} (u - W/2)/f \\ -(v - H/2)/f \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} $$
    where $R_i$ is derived from the rotation representation (e.g., axis-angle via Rodrigues' formula) [7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md].
2.  **Joint Gradient Flow:** The rendering loss $\mathcal{L}$ (typically photometric) is backpropagated through the volume rendering integral to update both the NeRF weights $\Theta$ and the camera parameters $\pi_i = (R_i, t_i, f)$ [7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md].
3.  **Optimization Loop:** Standard optimizers (e.g., Adam) update $\Theta$ and $\pi_i$ in parallel. Learning rates and decay schedules are often decoupled to stabilize convergence, as pose optimization is more sensitive to local minima than weight optimization [7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md].

## Subtopics

### [NeRF with Unknown Camera Parameters](7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md)
The baseline method for joint optimization. It treats camera extrinsics (axis-angle rotation and translation) and intrinsics (shared focal length) as learnable variables. It differs from [NoPe-NeRF](8705-nope-nerf.md) by relying solely on photometric consistency without geometric priors. It is chosen when SfM fails or is unavailable, but requires careful initialization to avoid local minima.

### [Hybrid 2D/3D Registration Optimization Pipeline](8120-hybrid-2d-3d-registration-optimization-pipeline.md)
A two-stage registration method for 2D/3D alignment (e.g., X-ray to CT). It uses a differentiable network loss for global convergence and switches to Gradient-based Normalized Cross-Correlation (Grad-NCC) for local refinement. It differs from pure NeRF methods by targeting medical image registration and leveraging the locally convex landscape of ZNCC. Choose this for rigid 2D/3D registration where network losses are insufficient for local precision.

### [NoPe-NeRF](8705-nope-nerf.md)
Optimizes NeRF and poses using undistorted monocular depth priors. It differs from the baseline by introducing a point cloud loss that constrains relative poses between consecutive frames, stabilizing optimization in challenging trajectories. Choose this when monocular depth estimation is reliable and photometric loss alone is ambiguous.

### [AltNeRF](8763-altnerf.md)
An alternating optimization framework decoupling Scene Prior Module (SPM) and Scene Representation Module (SRM). It differs from joint optimization methods by iteratively refining depth/pose priors and NeRF weights separately, using error-tolerant regularization. Choose this for monocular videos where explicit 3D supervision is needed but direct joint optimization is unstable.

### [Vision-Only Pose Filtering in a NeRF](10501-vision-only-pose-filtering-in-a-nerf.md)
A recursive Bayesian filter for 6DoF pose and velocity estimation using a pre-trained NeRF. It differs from training methods by integrating system dynamics and projecting onto the SE(3) manifold after every gradient step. Choose this for real-time robot localization where a static NeRF model is available.

### [Online Receding Horizon Replanning](10509-online-receding-horizon-replanning.md)
A navigation pipeline combining trajectory planning and pose filtering in a receding horizon loop. It differs from static planning by allowing homotopy changes in response to disturbances. Choose this for dynamic robot navigation in NeRF-represented environments with uncertain initial poses.

### [NeRF-based Trajectory Optimization](10632-nerf-based-trajectory-optimization.md)
Plans collision-free trajectories by optimizing flat output waypoints using NeRF density as a collision proxy. It differs from pose estimation by optimizing a sequence of states for a differentially flat system (e.g., quadrotor). Choose this for motion planning in complex environments using implicit obstacle representations.

### NeRF Registration
A rigid registration method minimizing photometric loss between two NeRFs using Viewshed Fields (VF) and Normalizing Flows to guide sampling [S1]. It optimizes a 6-DoF transformation and a learnable scale factor. Pitfalls include susceptibility to textureless surfaces, symmetry-induced 180° deviations, and failure with partial overlap or moving objects [S1].

### Progressive Camera Pose Generation
A training strategy that stabilizes optimization by gradually increasing the angular distance of sampled target viewpoints. It adds noise uniformly from $[-\beta, +\beta]$ to Euler rotation angles, with $\beta$ growing linearly from 3 to 9 degrees [S2, unofficial]. This prevents negative effects from sampling far poses too early.

## Background
The problem of optimizing camera poses alongside NeRF parameters was first demonstrated in the original NeRF paper's "NeRF--" variant, which showed that joint optimization is possible but prone to local minima [7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md]. Subsequent work introduced geometric priors (monocular depth) to stabilize this process [8705-nope-nerf.md][8763-altnerf.md]. The field has expanded to include hybrid registration pipelines for medical imaging [8120-hybrid-2d-3d-registration-optimization-pipeline.md] and dynamic robot navigation using NeRFs as measurement models [10501-vision-only-pose-filtering-in-a-nerf.md][10509-online-receding-horizon-replanning.md][10632-nerf-based-trajectory-optimization.md].
